matching_rule.key: last two '::' components (Class::Method), template args stripped -- the same key tools/re/hasbody.py uses, because our namespaces do not always match the console canonical name. Consequence: overloads, and same-named classes in different namespaces, COLLAPSE onto one key.
matching_rule.definition: a declarator followed by '{' (or by a ctor ':' init list), in-class or out-of-class, in any .h/.cpp under b5-decomp/src
matching_rule.declaration: a declarator followed by ';' at CLASS scope; '= 0' / '= delete' / '= default' / template declarations excluded
call_site_strong: Class::Method(  where the qualifier is the class, a base, or a derived class
&Class::Method, or &Method inside a method of the family
bare Method( inside a method of the class or of a base/derived class
recv->Method( / recv.Method( where recv resolves to the family through a tree-wide 'Type name' / 'Type *name' / 'Type &name' binding
fn()->Method( / fn().Method( where fn's return type resolves to the family
this->Method( inside a method of the family
matching_rule.call_site_weak: any other same-named ->Method( / .Method( / bare Method( -- counted per row as unattributed_same_name_calls and DISCLOSED, never treated as a call site

known_blind_spots: VIRTUAL DISPATCH: a console virtual is reached through a vtable and carries NO xrefs_to, so it lands in console-orphan even if the game calls it every frame. 25.3% of all 30,084 console functions have an empty xrefs_to. Resolving those needs tools/re/vcallsites.py / vdispatch_audit.py per slot; this sweep does not do it, so console-orphan is NOT proof of 'nothing calls it'.
ICF FOLDING: identical one-line console bodies are folded, so IDA can print a neighbour's name on the fold target.
INLINING ON OUR SIDE: if we inlined the console function into its caller, 'no definition' is correct and there is no defect. Per-row judgement.
OVERLOADS / NAMESPACE COLLISIONS collapse on the Class::Method key -- in the SAFE direction (a same-named body elsewhere makes us say HAS BODY, under-reporting).
MOUNTING: a body in b5-decomp/src does not mean its TU is mounted into the exe build (tools/build/build_game_exe.bat).
REACHABILITY: a console caller having a body here does not prove that body runs.
MACROS: preprocessor directives are blanked, so a call generated by a macro body is invisible to the call index.
